input_references.role: Timestamped trajectory points with matched corridor coordinates, speed, direction, and mode

metadata.goal: Analyze the user's repeated travel patterns across the provided trajectories and identify regularities and variations in movement behavior.
metadata.category: Repeated corridor geometry, directional efficiency, and exceptions
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed single-user WorldTrace case containing 200 trips across 100 weekdays on one recurrent bidirectional corridor. Each day contains a morning A-to-B trip and an evening B-to-A trip; car travel dominates, with four cycling and four walking commute days.

insight_list.insight: Most repeated trips connect the same origin–destination pair in both directions, following recurrent direction-specific road-route families.

plot.title: Recurrent Corridor Directional Efficiency: Insight 1
plot.description: The question-specific evidence is computed from the synchronized trajectory and point tables; the case-level overview map is not repeated for this insight.

insight_list.question: Do repeated trips between the same endpoints follow recurrent direction-specific road-route families?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare the relevant direction groups using the synchronized trajectory summaries and matched-road geometry.

insight_list.insight: Within this recurrent corridor, travel direction is associated with movement efficiency: trips in one direction generally show lower mean speeds and higher route-indirectness scores than trips in the reverse direction.

plot.title: Recurrent Corridor Directional Efficiency: Insight 2
plot.description: The question-specific evidence is computed from the synchronized trajectory and point tables; the case-level overview map is not repeated for this insight.

insight_list.question: How do speed and route indirectness differ between regular A-to-B and B-to-A trips?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare the relevant direction groups using the synchronized trajectory summaries and matched-road geometry.

insight_list.insight: A small number of trips deviate from the dominant directional pattern, remaining unusually fast and direct in the direction that is otherwise characterized by slower and less direct travel.

plot.title: Recurrent Corridor Directional Efficiency: Insight 3
plot.description: The question-specific evidence is computed from the synchronized trajectory and point tables; the case-level overview map is not repeated for this insight.

insight_list.question: Are there rare A-to-B trips that remain unusually fast and direct?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare the relevant direction groups using the synchronized trajectory summaries and matched-road geometry.

insights: Most repeated trips connect the same origin–destination pair in both directions, following recurrent direction-specific road-route families.

Within this recurrent corridor, travel direction is associated with movement efficiency: trips in one direction generally show lower mean speeds and higher route-indirectness scores than trips in the reverse direction.
A small number of trips deviate from the dominant directional pattern, remaining unusually fast and direct in the direction that is otherwise characterized by slower and less direct travel.
summary: Repeated trips largely share one bidirectional corridor. Regular A-to-B travel is slower and less direct than B-to-A travel, with three rare A-to-B trips forming fast and direct exceptions.
